0: AN ORDINANCE TO PROVIDE FOR THE APPOINTMENT OF JUDGES OF THE MUNICIPAL COURT OF PINE MOUNTAIN, GEORGIA; TO PROVIDE FOR A TERM OF OFFICE FOR SUCH JUDGES; TO PROVIDE AN EFFECTIVE DATE; TO REPEAL ALL ORDINANCES AND PARTS OF ORDINANCES IN CONFLICT HEREWITH; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
1:
- (a) All judges of the Municipal Court of Pine Mountain, Georgia shall be appointed by Resolution of the Town Council and shall serve a term of one year, which term, and any successive term(s) shall be automatically extended for an additional one year term unless terminated by either party in its sole discretion by a written termination notice delivered no less than thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of any such term.

- (b) The appointment of each judge shall be as set forth in a separate contract with such judge signed by the Mayor with the consent of the Town Council as memorialized by adoption of a Resolution. A copy of this Ordinance shall be attached to each such contract and each such contract shall incorporate all terms of this Ordinance by express reference and shall set forth the agreed compensation of such judge during the term(s) of such contract.

- (c) The position of judge created in this Ordinance shall not be a full-time position, and the person serving in said position may engage in the private practice of law; provided, however, that a sitting judge may not appear and represent a client before the Municipal Court of Pine Mountain, Georgia.

- (d) No person shall be qualified or eligible to serve as a judge of the Municipal Court of Pine Mountain, Georgia unless he or she shall be in compliance with the requirements of state law setting forth the minimum qualifications necessary to serve in such office.

- (e) Before beginning the duties of his or her office, appointed judges shall take an oath before an officer duly authorized to administer oaths in this state declaring that he or she will truly, honestly, and faithfully discharge the

duties of his or her office to the best of his or her ability without fear, favor or partiality. The oath shall be entered upon the minutes of the Town Council.

- (f) | Subject to subsection (a) above, judges of the Municipal Court of Pine Mountain, Georgia shall serve for the designated term(s), provided that they may be removed at any time from the position by a two-thirds vote of the entire membership of the Town Council or upon action taken by the State Judicial Qualifications Commission for:

- (1) Willful misconduct in office;

- (2) Willful and persistent failure to perform duties;

- (3) Habitual intemperance;

- (4) Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice which brings the judicial office and the Municipal Court of Pine Mountain, Georgia into disrepute;

- (5) Disability seriously interfering with the performance of duties, which is, or is likely to become, of a permanent character; or

- (6) Such further prohibited action (or failure to act) as the Town Council may define by Charter Amendment.

Procedures for any such removal shall be set forth in 0.C.G.A. §36-

32-2.1.

SECTION TWO All Ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby expressly repealed.

SECTION THREE This Ordinance shall become effective on April 10, 2017.
8:
- (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter or any general or local Act, the governing authority of each municipal corporation within this state having a municipal court, as provided by the Act incorporating the municipal corporation or any amendments thereto, is authorized to appoint a judge of such court. Any individual appointed as a judge under this Code section shall possess such qualifications as set forth in Code Section 36-32-1.1 and shall receive such compensation as shall be fixed by the governing authority of the municipal corporation. Any individual appointed as a judge under this Code section shall serve for a minimum term of one year and until a successor is appointed or if the judge is removed from office as provided in Code Section 36-32-2.1. Such term shall be memorialized in a written agreement between such individual and the governing authority of the municipal corporation or in an ordinance or a charter. With respect to an individual serving as a municipal court judge in a consolidated government, the local Act shall determine the term of such judge.

- (b) This Code section shall not be construed to require the governing authority of any municipal corporation to appoint a judge; but such governing authority may appoint a judge if, acting in its sole discretion, the governing authority determines that such appointment would be in the best interest of the municipal corporation.
